questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between how a sandbox and a scratch org are created?
options: A sandbox is copied from an existing org's metadata (and sometimes data); a scratch org is built from nothing using a definition file and source in version control
There is no real difference -- both are copied from production
A scratch org is copied from production, while a sandbox is built from a definition file
Sandboxes and scratch orgs are both created exclusively through the Salesforce CLI
questions.explain: A sandbox inherits whatever configuration an existing org already has; a scratch org starts empty and is built up only from source applied against a scratch org definition file.

options: A third-party AppExchange package required to install Salesforce
A production or Developer Edition org enabled to create and manage scratch orgs
A type of sandbox with unlimited storage
The Salesforce support team's internal ticketing system
questions.explain: Scratch orgs are created from a Dev Hub using Salesforce CLI commands against a project's source and its scratch org definition file.

questions.q: What are the default and maximum lifespans for a scratch org?
options: Default 30 days, maximum 90 days
Default 1 day, maximum 7 days
Default 7 days, maximum 30 days
Scratch orgs never expire unless manually deleted
questions.explain: A scratch org's duration is chosen at creation in days, with a default of 7 and a maximum of 30; once it expires it cannot be restored.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe scratch org expiration as a deliberate design feature rather than a limitation?
options: Because it prevents developers from ever testing Apex code
Because it saves Salesforce money on server costs
Because expiration only affects scratch orgs created on weekends
Because guaranteed disappearance forces the discipline that nothing important can live only inside a scratch org -- everything of value must be captured in version control
questions.explain: Since a scratch org is guaranteed to vanish, nothing valuable can be allowed to exist only inside it -- which enforces exactly the source-driven discipline this development style depends on.

questions.q: A team wants to move from long-lived Developer sandboxes with years of unrecorded configuration to a scratch-org-based approach. What risk does this lesson say they must address first?
options: There is no risk -- scratch orgs automatically import all existing sandbox configuration on creation
Scratch orgs cannot be used by any team that has ever used a sandbox
If their existing configuration was never fully captured in version control, a scratch org built purely from that source will be missing whatever wasn't captured
Moving to scratch orgs requires deleting all existing sandboxes first
questions.explain: A scratch org only contains what's applied from source -- if the sandbox's accumulated configuration was never actually committed to version control, that gap will surface as missing functionality in the scratch org.
